title: Leader of Israel's Host, and Guide
description: Leader of Israel's Host, and Guide in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 270, “God Leads Us Right”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lea-der of Is-rael's host, and Guide Of all who seek the land a-bove, Be-neath Thy sha-dow we a-bide, The cloud of Thy pro-tect-ing love; Our strength Thy grace, our rule Thy word, Our end the glo-ry of the Lord.

lines: Leader of Israel's host, and Guide
Of all who seek the land above,
The cloud of Thy protecting love;
Our strength Thy grace, our rule Thy word,
Our end the glory of the Lord.
We shall not in the desert stray,
We shall not full direction need,
As far from danger as from fear,
While love, almighty love, is near.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
